claims.text: Stochastic incorporation of multiple transition metals produces isolated Pt and Pd active sites in noble-metal-based HEA nanocatalysts.
Adjacent cheaper transition metals donate charge to isolated Pt and Pd sites.
Charge transfer from adjacent metals modifies the d-band electronic structure of Pt and Pd.
The modified d-band structure enhances chemisorption of reactants such as nitrobenzene.
Enhanced reactant chemisorption results in improved catalytic performance.
The proposed PtPdCoCuNi nanoparticles are uniformly dispersed on SiO2.
Pt and Pd are atomically isolated within the PtPdCoCuNi multimetal matrix.
A PtPdCoCuNi HEA can be compared with a binary PtPd alloy synthesized under identical solvothermal conditions.
A disordered multimetal matrix promotes inter-element charge transfer.
Limited atomic mobility and random multielement incorporation favor separation of noble-metal atoms by cheaper transition metals.
Electron donation to Pt and Pd shifts their d-band center.
The d-band-center shift enhances substrate adsorption and reaction turnover.
Under identical reaction conditions, PtPdCoCuNi HEA catalysts will produce more than twice the nitrobenzene yield of binary PtPd catalysts.
The proposed effect is expected to hold for synthesis routes that limit atomic mobility, including solvothermal synthesis.
The proposed effect is expected for reactions requiring isolated noble-metal sites, including nitrobenzene hydrogenation below 100 °C.
XPS binding-energy shifts can provide evidence of charge transfer involving Pt and Pd.
Failure to observe Pt/Pd binding-energy shifts, increased site isolation, and enhanced catalytic performance relative to PtPd would falsify the proposed mechanism.
